name: Subdermal Ferroelectric Shear Projector
description: The Subdermal Ferroelectric Shear Projector fires a focused, rapidly alternating ferroelectric field pulse that penetrates the skin and induces mechanical shear stress in ferromagnetic and piezoelectric materials implanted beneath it — specifically the titanium alloy housings, ceramic substrates, and magnetostrictive actuators common in cybernetic implants. The effect on a heavily augmented target is catastrophic: implant housings fracture along stress lines, flexible circuit substrates delaminate, and the physical interface between biological tissue and synthetic components is violently disrupted. On unaugmented targets, the weapon produces a deep bruising sensation and mild muscle spasm, little more.
legality: Licensed — civilian ownership prohibited; law enforcement and licensed security use permitted under Augmentation Compliance Framework regulations
specifications:
effective range: 20 meters (full effect), 35 meters (partial effect)
field pulse frequency: Variable 50–200 Hz alternating
charge levels: Three — Compliance (mild disruption), Suppress (moderate shear), Destroy (catastrophic implant failure)
effect on unaugmented: Minor — deep tissue vibration, transient muscle spasm
effect on heavily augmented: Severe — implant structural failure, biological interface disruption, possible internal hemorrhage at implant sites
weight: 3.8 kg
shots per cell: 20 at Compliance, 12 at Suppress, 6 at Destroy
implant scanner range: 5 meters passive
tactical_use: Deployed in augmentation-heavy environments where standard lethal weapons create legal liability but operators anticipate encountering heavily modified targets. The Compliance setting is used for crowd work and initial contact. Suppress is used when a target is actively resisting. Destroy is technically reserved for imminent threat scenarios but has been used in documented incidents under disputed circumstances. Counter-augmentation specialists pair the SFSP-4 with conventional sidearms — the Cleaver disrupts a target's combat implants, and the sidearm handles the follow-up.
cultural_context: The SFSP-4 has become the single most politically charged weapon in GLMZ's current public discourse. For the city's augmented population — which in some districts constitutes a majority — it represents a weapon designed specifically to harm their bodies in ways the law does not fully recognize as assault. 'Cleaver' is used as both a noun and a verb in augmented communities: to be 'Cleavered' means to have your implants damaged by state or corporate force. Ringo Corponation's public affairs team insists the weapon is non-lethal and that documented deaths following SFSP-4 use were caused by pre-existing conditions, not the weapon. This position has not improved their standing.
story_hooks: A Ringo Corponation internal memo has leaked suggesting the company knew the SFSP-4's implant scanner had a documented flaw that caused it to register bystanders as primary targets under certain lighting conditions — and shipped the weapon anyway. Someone wants the party to verify the memo's authenticity before it goes to a journalist.

A member of the party has had their implants damaged by an SFSP-4 hit — not in combat, but in what was supposedly a routine compliance stop. The officer who fired it claims the targeting scanner flagged the character as a high-augmentation threat. The scanner logs have been wiped.

An augmented community in the labor districts has obtained three SFSP-4 units through unclear means and is planning to use them against Ringo Corponation security during a planned protest action. The party must decide whether to intervene, facilitate, or stay out of it — and who they'll make enemies of either way.

physical_description.visual_profile: A stocky, brutalist pulse projector with a distinctly medical-industrial aesthetic. The weapon resembles a hybrid between a clinical diagnostic tool and a compact carbine, with a pronounced muzzle assembly housing the ferroelectric emitter array. The overall silhouette is blocky and functional, lacking traditional firearm grace—it reads as purpose-built enforcement hardware.
physical_description.dimensions: 46 cm length, 12 cm width at widest point (emitter housing), 8 cm height. Muzzle assembly protrudes 8 cm from the frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and deliberate in hand—3.8 kg distributed forward toward the emitter array, creating a front-heavy balance. Not unwieldy, but demands controlled grip and forearm stability. Feels like professional equipment, not consumer hardware.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer frame with embedded ferroelectric ceramic matrix in the emitter housing. Titanium alloy heat sink fins along the muzzle to dissipate field projection energy. Magnesium alloy receiver plate.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with brushed titanium accents. The ceramic emitter face has a faint iridescent sheen—visible evidence of the ferroelectric material beneath. Wear reveals lighter polymer underneath, typical of field-used compliance gear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with brushed steel/titanium accents. A single accent stripe of reflective warning yellow runs along the emitter housing—standard safety marking for electromagnetic discharge weapons.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressive textured rubberized polymer with subtle finger wells molded into the material. Designed for secure retention even in sweaty or augmented hands. The rear grip panel is slightly raised to accommodate gloved fingers.
distinctive_features: Prominent ferroelectric ceramic emitter matrix at muzzle—visible as a slightly proud, hexagonal array with faint rainbow iridescence
Three rotary selector switches on the left side labeled COMPLIANCE / SUPPRESS / DESTROY with corresponding LED indicators (green/yellow/red)
Passive implant-density scanner LED ring around the muzzle—activates in pale blue when scanning for metallic implants within 5 meters
Heat sink fins along the muzzle assembly, machined from titanium
Charge level indicator window on the upper receiver showing battery percentage via gradated bar
Recessed charging port on the right side with weatherproofed rubber cap
Serial/batch marking etched on the left receiver: 'SZI-SFSP4-[CODE]' with manufacture date
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sovereign Zone Insurance corporate logo embossed subtly on the left side of the polymer frame—a circular shield with geometric layering. Smaller regulatory stamps below: 'LICENSED ENFORCEMENT ONLY' and the GLMZ Augmentation Compliance Framework certification seal. Lot number and manufacture date lasered onto the rear receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly field-worn. Scuff marks on the polymer from duty belt contact. The muzzle assembly shows micro-scratches from repeated scanning passes. Battery contacts show minimal corrosion—equipment kept in regular service rotation. Occasionally seen with custom grip tape or augmented user markings, but factory-stock examples dominate law enforcement inventories.
